title: TypeScript functions versus C# methods and delegates
hook: TypeScript functions are first-class values with structural typing; C# methods live on types and delegates provide typed function pointers with nominal conversion rules. Both erase to runtime behavior — but the compile-time models differ sharply.

sections.heading: Functions in TS vs methods in C#

blocks.text: TypeScript **functions** are values — assignable to variables, passed as arguments, returned from other functions. **No overloading at runtime** — one emitted function per implementation. C# **methods** belong to classes/structs; **delegates** (`Func<T,R>`, `Action<T>`) are typed function references with nominal assignment rules. TS uses **structural** function types — any matching lambda fits. C# lambdas convert to delegates if signatures match the target delegate type.

entries.plainDefinition: Functions are values — not tied to a class.
Nominal typed reference to a method or lambda.

blocks.text: Full-stack engineers map Express middleware to ASP.NET middleware, LINQ Select to array.map, and event handlers across stacks. Misconception: 'TS methods work like C# virtual methods at type level' — TS uses structural matching. Async: C# async/await returns Task; TS returns Promise — similar ergonomics, different runtime (thread pool vs event loop).

blocks.body: static methods exist at runtime but delegate patterns use plain functions or object literals with call signatures.

blocks.title: Expecting nominal delegate safety
blocks.body: Any structurally matching function assigns in TS — use branded types or wrappers for domain separation.

blocks.text: C# local functions vs TS nested functions — both close over locals. Expression trees (C#) have no TS equivalent — metaprogramming uses types not expressions. IAsyncEnumerable vs AsyncIterable. Multicast delegates vs single function reference in JS. TS strictFunctionTypes closer to delegate variance on callbacks.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected
blocks.body: Saying TS overloads are like C# CLR overloads. Not mapping Func/Action. Ignoring this-binding when passing methods.

interviewTakeaways: TS functions are first-class, structurally typed values.
C# delegates are nominal — Func/Action map to (T) => R.
TS overloads compile to one function; C# emits multiple methods.
60s: TS structural functions vs C# nominal delegates. map = Select. Promise = Task. Mind this when passing methods. No expression trees in TS.
commonPitfalls: Weak: TS methods are nominal like C# — structural matching.
Weak: ignoring this when passing instance methods as callbacks.
Strong: Map Func/Action to function types. Structural assignability. async Promise vs Task. bind/arrow for this.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS pioneered first-class functions — TS and C# both build on that JS runtime model in the browser/Node.
Unlike C# delegate nominal typing, any matching function shape assigns — know when to add branded wrappers.
